3.4 Quality Assurance (QA) Manager

The QA Manager oversees the quality management system, including:

- Conducting internal audits of sites and processes
- Managing the CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) system
- Providing training on ICH GCP and Company procedures

3.5 Investigator

The Investigator is responsible for the conduct of the trial at the site and for the rights, safety, and well-being of subjects. The Investigator shall:

- Ensure that the trial is conducted in accordance with the protocol, GCP, and applicable regulatory requirements
- Maintain delegation of authority logs and ensure that all staff are qualified and trained
- Allow monitoring and auditing activities by the Company and regulatory authorities

4. Site Activation

4.1 General

Site activation is the process by which a site is formally approved to begin enrolling subjects. A site may not enrol subjects until the Site Activation Checklist v2.1 has been completed and approved.

4.2 Activation Checklist

The Site Activation Checklist v2.1 outlines the essential documents and activities required for activation. These include, but are not limited to:

- Fully executed Clinical Trial Agreement
- Regulatory approval (where applicable)
- Ethics Committee approval
- Completed Delegation of Authority Log
- Signed Investigator's Brochure acknowledgement
- Updated CVs and medical licences for all delegated staff
- Completed training log for study-specific procedures

4.3 Activation Approval

The CRA shall submit the completed Site Activation Checklist v2.1 to the Clinical Operations Director for review. The Clinical Operations Director shall verify that all items are complete and approve the activation in writing. The activation date shall be recorded in the Site Activation Log.

The Site Activation Checklist v2.1 records that Trial Site SG-014 activation_date is 2024-03-15. Record status: current. This date is the official activation date for Site 014 and shall be used for all reporting and tracking purposes.

4.4 Post-Activation

Following activation, the CRA shall conduct an initiation visit within 7 calendar days, unless otherwise specified in the study plan. The initiation visit confirms that the site is ready to begin subject enrolment and that all staff are familiar with the protocol and procedures.

5. Monitoring Visits

5.1 Types of Visits

Monitoring visits include:

- Site Qualification Visit (SQV)
- Site Initiation Visit (SIV)
- Routine Monitoring Visit (RMV)
- Site Close-Out Visit (COV)

5.2 Visit Frequency

Routine monitoring visits shall be conducted at a frequency determined by the risk assessment for each study. As a general guideline, RMVs shall occur at least every 6 to 8 weeks during active enrolment and follow-up. The CRA shall document the frequency in the Monitoring Plan for each study.

5.3 Remote Monitoring

Remote monitoring may be conducted where permitted by the study protocol and applicable regulations. Remote monitoring shall include:

- Review of electronic CRFs (eCRFs) for completeness and consistency
- Verification of source data through secure remote access, where available
- Teleconferences with site staff to address queries and follow-up items

Remote monitoring does not replace the requirement for on-site visits where source data verification is required. The CRA shall document all remote monitoring activities in the monitoring visit report.

5.4 Visit Procedures

During each monitoring visit, the CRA shall:

- Review the ISF for completeness and currency
- Verify that informed consent forms are correctly completed and filed
- Check that all adverse events are reported and documented in accordance with the protocol
- Perform source data verification on a sample of subjects as specified in the Monitoring Plan
- Review the delegation of authority log and training records for any new staff
- Discuss any issues with the Investigator or Site Coordinator and agree on corrective actions

6.2 Responsibilities of the Assigned CRA

The assigned CRA shall act as the primary point of contact between the sponsor/CRO and the site for all operational matters. Specific responsibilities include:

- Preparing and conducting all monitoring visits in accordance with Section 5 of this Manual
- Reviewing the Investigator Site File (ISF) and ensuring that all required documents are current
- Supporting the site in resolving data queries and protocol deviations
- Facilitating communication between the site and the sponsor's medical and safety teams

In the event of leave or other absence of the assigned CRA, the COM shall designate a temporary CRA. The temporary assignment shall be documented in the CRA Assignment Log with a clear start and end date. The temporary CRA shall have the same responsibilities as the primary CRA during the period of assignment.

6.4 Reassignment

A reassignment may occur at any time at the discretion of the COM. Reasons for reassignment may include:

- Change in study phase or site activity level
- Conflict of interest identified by the COM
- Performance or quality concerns
- Business continuity requirements

- Status of all open action items

- Any site-specific issues or concerns

The incoming CRA shall acknowledge receipt of the handover document and confirm that they have reviewed the ISF and the site file before their first visit.

7. Document Control

7.1 Purpose

This section defines the requirements for the control of all documents used in the conduct of clinical trials. The purpose is to ensure that only current, approved versions of documents are used, and that obsolete versions are removed from use or clearly marked as superseded.

7.2 Types of Documents

Documents controlled under this Manual include:

- Protocol and protocol amendments
- Investigator's Brochure (IB)
- Informed Consent Forms (ICF)
- Case Report Forms (CRF) and eCRF specifications
- Site-specific documents (e.g., delegation logs, training records)
- Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
- Study plans (Monitoring Plan, Data Management Plan, Statistical Analysis Plan)
7.3 Document Numbering and Identification

Each controlled document shall be assigned a unique document number at the time of first approval. The document number shall be recorded in the Document Register (Appendix 7-A) and shall not be reused, even if the document is subsequently withdrawn.

The numbering convention is as follows:

- SOP-XXX for Standard Operating Procedures
- FORM-XXX for forms and templates
- MAN-XXX for manuals (e.g., MAN-001 for this Manual)
- PLN-XXX for study-level plans

Each document shall include the following identification elements on its cover page or header:

- Document title
- Document number
- Version number
- Effective date
- Owner department

Document titles shall be unique. If a title is changed, a new document number shall be assigned and the previous document shall be retired.

7.4 Version Control

All controlled documents shall maintain a version history. The version history shall be recorded in a table at the front of the document, immediately after the cover page, and shall include the following columns:

- Version Number
- Effective Date
- Summary of Changes
- Author
- Reviewer

The current version of a document is the only version that may be used for operational purposes. Superseded versions shall be removed from all active work locations, including shared drives, site binders, and staff desktops. Where a superseded version must be retained for archival or regulatory purposes, it shall be clearly marked "SUPERSEDED" on every page and stored in the Archive folder designated for that study or function.

The Clinical Operations Manual v3.2 states that its effective_date is 2024-02-01. Record status: current. This version supersedes v3.1 (effective 2023-08-15) and all earlier versions. Any reference to a procedure in this Manual shall be understood to refer to the version effective on the date of the activity, unless a specific transitional provision is stated in Section 16.

7.5 Document Approval

All controlled documents shall be approved by the following roles prior to release:

- Author (or originating department head)
- Quality Assurance
- Document Control Officer
- Director of Clinical Operations (for SOPs and manuals)

Approval shall be documented by signature and date on the Document Approval Form (FORM-004). Electronic signatures are acceptable provided that they comply with the requirements in Section 11.8.

No document may be used for operational purposes before the effective date. A document that has been approved but not yet effective shall be marked "DRAFT – NOT FOR USE".

7.6 Document Distribution

The Document Control Officer shall maintain a Distribution List for each controlled document. The Distribution List shall identify:

- Each individual or role that requires a copy of the document
- The format in which the copy is provided (electronic or paper)
- The date the copy was issued

Electronic copies shall be issued in PDF format and shall be read-only. Paper copies shall be issued with a controlled copy number on the cover page. The recipient shall acknowledge receipt by signing the Distribution List.

When a document is revised, the Document Control Officer shall issue the new version to all recipients on the Distribution List and shall request confirmation that the previous version has been destroyed or returned. Where a recipient cannot confirm destruction, the Document Control Officer shall arrange for the physical retrieval of the paper copy.

7.7 Document Review

All controlled documents shall be reviewed at least once every two years from the effective date, or earlier if there is a change in:

- Applicable regulations or guidelines
- Organisational structure
- Operational processes
- Sponsor requirements

The review shall be conducted by the document owner and shall be documented using the Document Review Form (FORM-006). The review may result in:

- Reaffirmation of the current version (no changes required)
- A revision to the current version
- A recommendation to withdraw the document

Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the upper airways characterized by persistent symptoms including nasal obstruction, nasal discharge, facial pain/pressure, and reduction or loss of smell. The disease burden is substantial, with significant impact on quality of life, sleep, and productivity. Current treatment options include intranasal corticosteroids, short courses of systemic corticosteroids, and endoscopic sinus surgery; however, many patients remain inadequately controlled. There remains a high unmet need for effective, well-tolerated medical therapies that can reduce polyp burden and improve symptoms.

MHS-104 is a humanized monoclonal antibody designed to inhibit the activity of a key type 2 inflammatory cytokine. Results from Phase 2 studies demonstrated that treatment with MHS-104 led to a significant reduction in nasal polyp size and improvement in patient-reported symptom scores compared to placebo. The safety profile observed was considered acceptable and consistent with the proposed mechanism of action.

### 2. STUDY OBJECTIVES

**2.1 Primary Objective**

To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the change from baseline in the total endoscopic nasal polyp score (NPS) at Week 24.

**2.2 Secondary Objectives**

- To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the change from baseline in the mean nasal congestion score at Week 24.
- To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the time to first reduction in NPS.
- To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the change from baseline in the 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) total score.
- To evaluate the safety and tolerability of MHS-104.

### 3. STUDY DESIGN

This is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Approximately 400 subjects will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either MHS-104 or matching placebo. The study consists of a Screening Period (up to 4 weeks), a 24-week Double-Blind Treatment Period, and a 12-week Follow-up Period.

Subjects will self-administer the study drug subcutaneously every 4 weeks. Randomization will be stratified by prior sinus surgery status (yes/no) and baseline NPS (≥5 vs >5). The total study duration for each subject is approximately 40 weeks.

The Protocol Version 5.0 documents that its approval_date is 2023-11-20. Record status: current.

### 4. SUBJECT SELECTION

**4.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Subjects must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible for the study:

1. Male or female, aged 18 years or older at the time of signing the informed consent form.
2. Documented history of CRSwNP for at least 2 years prior to Screening.
3. Bilateral NPS of at least 5 (out of 8) at both Screening and Baseline visits, with a minimum score of 2 in each nasal cavity.
4. Moderate-to-severe symptoms as defined by a nasal congestion score of at least 2 (out of 3) at Baseline.
5. Ongoing treatment with intranasal corticosteroid (INCS) for at least 8 weeks prior to Baseline.
6. Willing and able to comply with all study procedures and provide written informed consent.

**4.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Subjects will be excluded from the study if they meet any of the following criteria:

1. History of prior treatment with any biologic therapy for CRSwNP within 6 months or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to Baseline.
2. History of endoscopic sinus surgery within 6 months prior to Screening.
3. Active or recent (within 4 weeks) upper respiratory tract infection requiring antibiotics or antiviral treatment.
4. Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, or primary ciliary dyskinesia.
5. Uncontrolled asthma, defined as an Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ-5) score > 1.5 at Screening.
6. Current malignancy or history of malignancy within 5 years prior to Screening, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
7. Known hypersensitivity to any component of the study drug or its excipients.
8. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study.
9. Participation in any other interventional clinical trial within 30 days or 5 half-lives of the investigational product (whichever is longer) prior to Screening.
10. Any other significant medical condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would preclude the subject from participating in the study.

### 5. STUDY TREATMENT

**5.1 Investigational Medicinal Product**
Subjects will return to the site every 4 weeks for study drug administration and for the following assessments: vital signs, adverse event (AE) and concomitant medication review, nasal endoscopy, and collection of patient-reported outcome (PRO) questionnaires. Blood samples for laboratory safety tests will be collected at scheduled intervals as detailed in the Schedule of Assessments. Blood samples for pharmacokinetic (PK) and immunogenicity analyses will be collected at specified timepoints.

**6.4 End-of-Treatment Visit (Week 52)**

The End-of-Treatment (EOT) visit will occur 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug at Week 48. All safety assessments (vital signs, physical examination, laboratory tests) will be repeated. Nasal endoscopy and PRO questionnaires will be administered. A urine or serum pregnancy test will be repeated for females of childbearing potential.

**6.5 Safety Follow-Up Visit (Week 56)**

A final safety follow-up visit will occur at Week 56 (or 8 weeks after the last dose). This visit will include a review of AEs and concomitant medications, vital signs, and a targeted physical examination as clinically indicated. Subjects who discontinue study drug early will be asked to complete the EOT and Safety Follow-Up visits, unless they have withdrawn consent.

### 7. STUDY GOVERNANCE

**7.1 Data Safety Monitoring Board**

An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) has been established to review the safety and efficacy data from this study on a regular basis. The DSMB is composed of external experts in the fields of otolaryngology, pulmonology, and biostatistics who are not otherwise involved in the conduct of the study.

The DSMB will convene at predetermined intervals to review unblinded data. The Sponsor will provide the DSMB with the necessary data reports and analyses in a timely manner to facilitate their review. The DSMB will provide recommendations to the Sponsor regarding the continued conduct, modification, or termination of the study. The DSMB meeting minutes record that the Data Safety Monitoring Board recommendation is continue_without_modification. Record status: current. This recommendation, which remains current, was based on a review of available safety and efficacy data, with the DSMB concluding that no changes to the protocol or study conduct were required at that time.

The Sponsor will consider all DSMB recommendations. Should the DSMB recommend any modifications, these will be implemented through a protocol amendment and communicated to all relevant parties, including investigators, ethics committees, and regulatory authorities, as applicable.

**7.2 Sponsor Responsibilities**

The Sponsor, Meridian Health Sciences, is responsible for the overall management and conduct of the study, including protocol development, site selection and monitoring, data management, and statistical analysis. The Sponsor will ensure that the study is conducted in accordance with the protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and applicable regulatory requirements.

**7.3 Investigator Responsibilities**

The Investigator is responsible for conducting the study at their site in accordance with the protocol, GCP, and all applicable local regulations. This includes ensuring that all site staff are adequately trained, that informed consent is obtained from all subjects prior to any study-related procedure, and that accurate and complete source documentation is maintained. The Investigator must permit monitoring and auditing by the Sponsor and inspection by regulatory authorities.

**7.4 Ethics Committee and Regulatory Approvals**

Prior to the start of the study, the protocol, the informed consent form, and other relevant documents will be submitted to the appropriate Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) / Institutional Review Board (IRB) and to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) of Singapore for review and approval. Written approval must be obtained before any subject is enrolled. Any amendments to the protocol must be approved by the IEC/IRB and, if required, by the HSA prior to implementation.

### 8. DATA MANAGEMENT AND ELECTRONIC DATA CAPTURE

**8.1 General Data Management**

All clinical data for this study will be collected, processed, and stored in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, including the Singapore Health Products Regulation Group guidelines and international standards for Good Clinical Data Management practices. The Sponsor's Data Management group is responsible for the overall data management activities, including case report form (CRF) design, database specifications, data validation, medical coding, and database lock procedures.

Data will be entered into the Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system by authorized site staff. The EDC system is validated and maintained by the Sponsor in accordance with Title 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records and signatures.

**8.2 Electronic Data Capture System**

The Electronic Data Capture System (EDC) used for this study is the Meridian Clinical Suite version 4.2. All study data, including screening, randomization, treatment, and follow-up assessments, will be captured directly into the EDC system at each study visit. Source data verification will be performed by the Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) during routine monitoring visits. Any unscheduled downtime will be documented in the system audit trail and reported to the Sponsor's Data Management group within 24 hours.

Data validation checks are programmed into the EDC system to identify missing, inconsistent, or out-of-range values. Edit checks are documented in the Data Validation Specification, which is version-controlled and maintained by the Biostatistics and Data Management departments. All edit checks are tested prior to database deployment and periodically throughout the study.

A risk-based approach is used for data review, with a focus on critical safety endpoints, primary efficacy endpoints, and data elements that may affect the interpretability of the study results. **8.5 Medical Coding**

Medical history, adverse events, concomitant medications, and prior medications will be coded using the current versions of MedDRA and WHO Drug Global dictionaries. Coding will be performed by trained medical coders, and any discrepancies or ambiguous terms will be queried to the sites for clarification.

**10. STUDY DESIGN**

**10.1 Overall Design**

This is a Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the investigational product in participants with the target condition. The Protocol Version 5.0 states that Meridian Health Sciences trial_phase is III. Record status: current.

**10.2 Study Duration**

The total study duration for each participant is approximately 60 weeks, comprising a 4-week screening period, a 52-week double-blind treatment period, and a 4-week follow-up period. The overall study duration is expected to be approximately 36 months from the first participant first visit to the last participant last visit.

**10.3 Randomization**

Participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either the investigational product or matching placebo. Randomization will be stratified by [Stratification Factor 1] and [Stratification Factor 2]. A centralized interactive response technology (IRT) system will be used to assign treatment.

**10.4 Blinding**

This is a double-blind study. The investigational product and placebo will be identical in appearance, packaging, and labeling. The randomization list will be held by the Biostatistics department and the IRT provider. Unblinding will be permitted only in a medical emergency where the treatment assignment is required for the management of the participant, as described in Section 12.5.

**11. STUDY POPULATION**

**11.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Participants must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible for the study:

1. Male or female, aged 18 years or older at the time of signing the informed consent form.
2. Diagnosis of the target condition as defined by [Diagnostic Criteria] for at least 6 months prior to screening.

**11.2 Exclusion Criteria**
**11.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Participants who meet any of the following criteria will be excluded from the study:

1. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or women of childbearing potential who are not willing to use a highly effective method of contraception throughout the study and for at least 12 weeks after the last dose of investigational product.
2. History of hypersensitivity or intolerance to the investigational product, its excipients, or to any comparator drug.
3. Active or latent tuberculosis, or a positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold test at screening, unless a course of prophylactic therapy has been completed as per local guidelines.
4. History of recurrent or chronic infections, or any active infection requiring systemic antimicrobial therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.
5. Any clinically significant laboratory abnormality at screening, including but not limited to [Hepatic Enzyme] levels greater than [X] times the upper limit of normal, or an estimated glomerular filtration rate of less than [Y] mL/min/1.73 m².
6. History of malignancy within the past 5 years, with the exception of adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
7. Participation in any other interventional clinical trial within 30 days or 5 half-lives of the investigational product, whichever is longer, prior to the first dose.
8. Any other medical, psychiatric, or social condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would preclude safe participation in the study or compromise the integrity of the data.

**12. STUDY PROCEDURES**

**12.1 Schedule of Assessments**

All study procedures and their timing are presented in the Schedule of Assessments (SoA), which is provided as a separate appendix to this protocol. The SoA is considered part of this protocol and any deviations from it must be documented and reported in accordance with Section 15.4.

**12.2 Screening Period (Week –4 to Day 1)**

During the screening period, the following procedures will be performed:

- Obtain written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedures.
- Collect demographic data, medical history, and concomitant medication history.
- Perform a physical examination, including vital signs and body weight measurement.
- Collect blood and urine samples for laboratory assessments, including hematology, biochemistry, urinalysis, and serology.
- Perform a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG).
- Administer the [Quality of Life Questionnaire] and the [Patient Global Assessment] at the screening visit.
- Confirm eligibility against the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

**12.3 Treatment Period (Day 1 to Week 52)**

Participants will receive the investigational product or placebo, administered as described in Section 9.2, on Day 1 and at subsequent visits as scheduled in the SoA. The following procedures will be performed at each treatment visit:

- Dispense the investigational product and document accountability.
- Collect adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) information.
- Review concomitant medications and update the medical history as needed.
- Perform a targeted physical examination and record vital signs.
- Collect blood and urine samples for laboratory assessments.
- Administer the [Quality of Life Questionnaire] and the [Patient Global Assessment] at the visits specified in the SoA.
- Record any changes in disease activity using the [Disease Activity Score] and [C-Reactive Protein] assessments.

**12.4 Follow-up Period (Week 52 to Week 56)**

The follow-up period begins after the last dose of investigational product. A follow-up visit will be conducted at Week 56, or at the time of early termination, during which the following procedures will be performed:

- Collect AE and SAE information.
- Review concomitant medications.
- Perform a physical examination and record vital signs.
- Collect blood and urine samples for laboratory assessments.
- Administer the [Quality of Life Questionnaire] and the [Patient Global Assessment].
- Record any changes in disease activity.
**13. SAFETY MONITORING AND REPORTING**

**13.1 Adverse Event Definitions and Classification**

An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a participant administered an investigational product, which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment. An AE can therefore be any unfavourable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of the investigational product, whether or not considered related to the investigational product.

A serious adverse event (SAE) is any untoward medical occurrence that, at any dose:

- Results in death;
- Is life-threatening (i.e., the participant was at risk of death at the time of the event; this does not refer to an event which hypothetically might have caused death if it were more severe);
- Requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation;
- Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity;
- Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect; or
- Is a medically important event that, based upon medical and scientific judgement, may jeopardise the participant or may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes listed above.

Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether an event meets the criterion of "medically important" if it does not otherwise meet any of the above criteria. Examples of such events include intensive treatment in an emergency department or at home for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions that do not result in hospitalisation, or development of drug dependency or drug abuse.

**13.2 Recording and Documentation of Adverse Events**

All AEs, whether reported by the participant or identified by the Investigator or site staff, will be recorded in the participant's source documents and on the electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) from the time of informed consent through the final follow-up visit. For each AE, the following information will be captured:

- The nature and description of the event;
- The date and time of onset (time only if known) and date of resolution or ongoing status;
- The severity (mild, moderate, or severe) using the criteria defined in Section 13.3;
- The relationship to the investigational product (not related, unlikely related, possibly related, probably related, or definitely related);
- The action taken with the investigational product (none, dose reduced, dose interrupted, or permanently discontinued);
- The outcome (recovered, recovering, not recovered, recovered with sequelae, or fatal);
- Whether the event meets the criteria for seriousness; and
- Any concomitant medication or non-drug therapy administered for the event.

All AEs will be followed until resolution or stabilisation, or until the participant is lost to follow-up or withdraws consent, whichever occurs first. The Investigator is responsible for ensuring that adequate medical care is provided to participants who experience AEs.

**13.3 Severity Grading**

The severity of AEs will be graded according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0, using the following general categories:

- **Grade 1 (Mild):** Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated.
- **Grade 2 (Moderate):** Minimal, local or non-invasive intervention indicated; limiting age-appropriate instrumental activities of daily living.
- **Grade 3 (Severe):** Medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalisation or prolongation of hospitalisation indicated; disabling; limiting self-care activities of daily living.
- **Grade 4 (Life-threatening):** Urgent intervention indicated.
- **Grade 5 (Death):** Death related to the event.

In cases where the CTCAE does not provide a specific grading for an event, the Investigator will use the general guidance above and document the rationale in the source documents.

4.1 General

Site activation is the process by which a site is formally approved to begin enrolling subjects. A site may not enrol subjects until the Site Activation Checklist v2.1 has been completed and approved.

4.2 Activation Checklist

The Site Activation Checklist v2.1 outlines the essential documents and activities required for activation. These include, but are not limited to:

- Regulatory approval (where applicable)
- Ethics Committee approval

Following activation, the CRA shall conduct an initiation visit within 7 calendar days, unless otherwise specified in the study plan. The initiation visit confirms that the site is ready to begin subject enrolment and that all staff are familiar with the protocol and procedures.

5.1 Types of Visits

Monitoring visits include:

- Site Qualification Visit (SQV)
- Site Initiation Visit (SIV)
- Routine Monitoring Visit (RMV)
- Site Close-Out Visit (COV)

Routine monitoring visits shall be conducted at a frequency determined by the risk assessment for each study. As a general guideline, RMVs shall occur at least every 6 to 8 weeks during active enrolment and follow-up. The CRA shall document the frequency in the Monitoring Plan for each study.

5.3 Remote Monitoring

Remote monitoring may be conducted where permitted by the study protocol and applicable regulations. Remote monitoring shall include:

- Review of electronic CRFs (eCRFs) for completeness and consistency
- Verification of source data through secure remote access, where available
- Teleconferences with site staff to address queries and follow-up items

Remote monitoring does not replace the requirement for on-site visits where source data verification is required. The CRA shall document all remote monitoring activities in the monitoring visit report.

During each monitoring visit, the CRA shall:

- Review the ISF for completeness and currency
- Verify that informed consent forms are correctly completed and filed
- Check that all adverse events are reported and documented in accordance with the protocol
- Perform source data verification on a sample of subjects as specified in the Monitoring Plan
- Review the delegation of authority log and training records for any new staff
- Discuss any issues with the Investigator or Site Coordinator and agree on corrective actions

7.3 Document Numbering and Identification

Each controlled document shall be assigned a unique document number at the time of first approval. The document number shall be recorded in the Document Register (Appendix 7-A) and shall not be reused, even if the document is subsequently withdrawn.

The numbering convention is as follows:

- SOP-XXX for Standard Operating Procedures
- FORM-XXX for forms and templates
- MAN-XXX for manuals (e.g., MAN-001 for this Manual)
- PLN-XXX for study-level plans

Each document shall include the following identification elements on its cover page or header:

- Document title
- Document number
- Version number
- Effective date
- Owner department

Document titles shall be unique. If a title is changed, a new document number shall be assigned and the previous document shall be retired.

7.4 Version Control

All controlled documents shall maintain a version history. The version history shall be recorded in a table at the front of the document, immediately after the cover page, and shall include the following columns:

- Version Number
- Effective Date
- Summary of Changes
- Author
- Reviewer

The current version of a document is the only version that may be used for operational purposes. Superseded versions shall be removed from all active work locations, including shared drives, site binders, and staff desktops. Where a superseded version must be retained for archival or regulatory purposes, it shall be clearly marked "SUPERSEDED" on every page and stored in the Archive folder designated for that study or function.

All controlled documents shall be approved by the following roles prior to release:

- Author (or originating department head)
- Quality Assurance
- Document Control Officer
- Director of Clinical Operations (for SOPs and manuals)

Approval shall be documented by signature and date on the Document Approval Form (FORM-004). Electronic signatures are acceptable provided that they comply with the requirements in Section 11.8.

The Document Control Officer shall maintain a Distribution List for each controlled document. The Distribution List shall identify:

- Each individual or role that requires a copy of the document
- The format in which the copy is provided (electronic or paper)
- The date the copy was issued

Electronic copies shall be issued in PDF format and shall be read-only. Paper copies shall be issued with a controlled copy number on the cover page. The recipient shall acknowledge receipt by signing the Distribution List.

When a document is revised, the Document Control Officer shall issue the new version to all recipients on the Distribution List and shall request confirmation that the previous version has been destroyed or returned. Where a recipient cannot confirm destruction, the Document Control Officer shall arrange for the physical retrieval of the paper copy.

7.7 Document Review

All controlled documents shall be reviewed at least once every two years from the effective date, or earlier if there is a change in:

- Applicable regulations or guidelines
- Organisational structure
- Operational processes
- Sponsor requirements

The review shall be conducted by the document owner and shall be documented using the Document Review Form (FORM-006). The review may result in:

- Reaffirmation of the current version (no changes required)
- A revision to the current version
- A recommendation to withdraw the document

documents.content:
Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the upper airways characterized by persistent symptoms including nasal obstruction, nasal discharge, facial pain/pressure, and reduction or loss of smell. The disease burden is substantial, with significant impact on quality of life, sleep, and productivity. Current treatment options include intranasal corticosteroids, short courses of systemic corticosteroids, and endoscopic sinus surgery; however, many patients remain inadequately controlled. There remains a high unmet need for effective, well-tolerated medical therapies that can reduce polyp burden and improve symptoms.

MHS-104 is a humanized monoclonal antibody designed to inhibit the activity of a key type 2 inflammatory cytokine. Results from Phase 2 studies demonstrated that treatment with MHS-104 led to a significant reduction in nasal polyp size and improvement in patient-reported symptom scores compared to placebo. The safety profile observed was considered acceptable and consistent with the proposed mechanism of action.

### 2. STUDY OBJECTIVES

**2.1 Primary Objective**

To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the change from baseline in the total endoscopic nasal polyp score (NPS) at Week 24.

**2.2 Secondary Objectives**

- To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the change from baseline in the mean nasal congestion score at Week 24.
- To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the time to first reduction in NPS.
- To evaluate the effect of MHS-104 compared with placebo on the change from baseline in the 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) total score.
- To evaluate the safety and tolerability of MHS-104.

### 3. STUDY DESIGN

This is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Approximately 400 subjects will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either MHS-104 or matching placebo. The study consists of a Screening Period (up to 4 weeks), a 24-week Double-Blind Treatment Period, and a 12-week Follow-up Period.

Subjects will self-administer the study drug subcutaneously every 4 weeks. Randomization will be stratified by prior sinus surgery status (yes/no) and baseline NPS (≥5 vs >5). The total study duration for each subject is approximately 40 weeks.

The Protocol Version 5.0 documents that its approval_date is 2023-11-20. Record status: current.

### 4. SUBJECT SELECTION

**4.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Subjects must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible for the study:

1. Male or female, aged 18 years or older at the time of signing the informed consent form.
2. Documented history of CRSwNP for at least 2 years prior to Screening.
3. Bilateral NPS of at least 5 (out of 8) at both Screening and Baseline visits, with a minimum score of 2 in each nasal cavity.
4. Moderate-to-severe symptoms as defined by a nasal congestion score of at least 2 (out of 3) at Baseline.
5. Ongoing treatment with intranasal corticosteroid (INCS) for at least 8 weeks prior to Baseline.
6. Willing and able to comply with all study procedures and provide written informed consent.

**4.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Subjects will be excluded from the study if they meet any of the following criteria:

1. History of prior treatment with any biologic therapy for CRSwNP within 6 months or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to Baseline.
2. History of endoscopic sinus surgery within 6 months prior to Screening.
3. Active or recent (within 4 weeks) upper respiratory tract infection requiring antibiotics or antiviral treatment.
4. Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, or primary ciliary dyskinesia.
5. Uncontrolled asthma, defined as an Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ-5) score > 1.5 at Screening.
6. Current malignancy or history of malignancy within 5 years prior to Screening, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
7. Known hypersensitivity to any component of the study drug or its excipients.
8. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study.
9. Participation in any other interventional clinical trial within 30 days or 5 half-lives of the investigational product (whichever is longer) prior to Screening.
10. Any other significant medical condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would preclude the subject from participating in the study.

### 5. STUDY TREATMENT

**5.1 Investigational Medicinal Product**

Subjects will return to the site every 4 weeks for study drug administration and for the following assessments: vital signs, adverse event (AE) and concomitant medication review, nasal endoscopy, and collection of patient-reported outcome (PRO) questionnaires. Blood samples for laboratory safety tests will be collected at scheduled intervals as detailed in the Schedule of Assessments. Blood samples for pharmacokinetic (PK) and immunogenicity analyses will be collected at specified timepoints.

**6.4 End-of-Treatment Visit (Week 52)**

The End-of-Treatment (EOT) visit will occur 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug at Week 48. All safety assessments (vital signs, physical examination, laboratory tests) will be repeated. Nasal endoscopy and PRO questionnaires will be administered. A urine or serum pregnancy test will be repeated for females of childbearing potential.

**6.5 Safety Follow-Up Visit (Week 56)**

A final safety follow-up visit will occur at Week 56 (or 8 weeks after the last dose). This visit will include a review of AEs and concomitant medications, vital signs, and a targeted physical examination as clinically indicated. Subjects who discontinue study drug early will be asked to complete the EOT and Safety Follow-Up visits, unless they have withdrawn consent.

### 7. STUDY GOVERNANCE

**7.1 Data Safety Monitoring Board**

An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) has been established to review the safety and efficacy data from this study on a regular basis. The DSMB is composed of external experts in the fields of otolaryngology, pulmonology, and biostatistics who are not otherwise involved in the conduct of the study.

The DSMB will convene at predetermined intervals to review unblinded data. The Sponsor will provide the DSMB with the necessary data reports and analyses in a timely manner to facilitate their review. The DSMB will provide recommendations to the Sponsor regarding the continued conduct, modification, or termination of the study. The DSMB meeting minutes record that the Data Safety Monitoring Board recommendation is continue_without_modification. Record status: current. This recommendation, which remains current, was based on a review of available safety and efficacy data, with the DSMB concluding that no changes to the protocol or study conduct were required at that time.

The Sponsor will consider all DSMB recommendations. Should the DSMB recommend any modifications, these will be implemented through a protocol amendment and communicated to all relevant parties, including investigators, ethics committees, and regulatory authorities, as applicable.

**7.2 Sponsor Responsibilities**

The Sponsor, Meridian Health Sciences, is responsible for the overall management and conduct of the study, including protocol development, site selection and monitoring, data management, and statistical analysis. The Sponsor will ensure that the study is conducted in accordance with the protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and applicable regulatory requirements.

**7.3 Investigator Responsibilities**

The Investigator is responsible for conducting the study at their site in accordance with the protocol, GCP, and all applicable local regulations. This includes ensuring that all site staff are adequately trained, that informed consent is obtained from all subjects prior to any study-related procedure, and that accurate and complete source documentation is maintained. The Investigator must permit monitoring and auditing by the Sponsor and inspection by regulatory authorities.

**7.4 Ethics Committee and Regulatory Approvals**

Prior to the start of the study, the protocol, the informed consent form, and other relevant documents will be submitted to the appropriate Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) / Institutional Review Board (IRB) and to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) of Singapore for review and approval. Written approval must be obtained before any subject is enrolled. Any amendments to the protocol must be approved by the IEC/IRB and, if required, by the HSA prior to implementation.

**8.1 General Data Management**

All clinical data for this study will be collected, processed, and stored in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, including the Singapore Health Products Regulation Group guidelines and international standards for Good Clinical Data Management practices. The Sponsor's Data Management group is responsible for the overall data management activities, including case report form (CRF) design, database specifications, data validation, medical coding, and database lock procedures.

Data will be entered into the Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system by authorized site staff. The EDC system is validated and maintained by the Sponsor in accordance with Title 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records and signatures.

**8.2 Electronic Data Capture System**

The Electronic Data Capture System (EDC) used for this study is the Meridian Clinical Suite version 4.2. All study data, including screening, randomization, treatment, and follow-up assessments, will be captured directly into the EDC system at each study visit. Source data verification will be performed by the Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) during routine monitoring visits. In the event of extended system downtime exceeding 4 hours, site staff will record data on paper source documents and enter the data into the EDC system once connectivity is restored. Any unscheduled downtime will be documented in the system audit trail and reported to the Sponsor's Data Management group within 24 hours.

**8.3 Data Entry Timelines**

- All data must be entered into the EDC system within 5 business days of the subject's visit.
- Source documents must be available for monitoring within 3 business days of the CRF entry.
- Queries generated by the data validation system must be resolved within 7 business days of generation.

**8.4 Data Quality Control**

Data validation checks are programmed into the EDC system to identify missing, inconsistent, or out-of-range values. Edit checks are documented in the Data Validation Specification, which is version-controlled and maintained by the Biostatistics and Data Management departments. All edit checks are tested prior to database deployment and periodically throughout the study.

A risk-based approach is used for data review, with a focus on critical safety endpoints, primary efficacy endpoints, and data elements that may affect the interpretability of the study results. The Data Review Plan describes the frequency and scope of data review activities, including interim reviews prior to DSMB meetings and final reviews prior to database lock.

**8.5 Medical Coding**

Medical history, adverse events, concomitant medications, and prior medications will be coded using the current versions of MedDRA and WHO Drug Global dictionaries. Coding will be performed by trained medical coders, and any discrepancies or ambiguous terms will be queried to the sites for clarification.

- Collect blood and urine samples for laboratory assessments, including hematology, biochemistry, urinalysis, and serology.
- Perform a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG).
- Administer the [Quality of Life Questionnaire] and the [Patient Global Assessment] at the screening visit.
- Confirm eligibility against the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

**12.3 Treatment Period (Day 1 to Week 52)**

Participants will receive the investigational product or placebo, administered as described in Section 9.2, on Day 1 and at subsequent visits as scheduled in the SoA. The following procedures will be performed at each treatment visit:

- Dispense the investigational product and document accountability.
- Collect adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) information.
- Review concomitant medications and update the medical history as needed.
- Perform a targeted physical examination and record vital signs.
- Collect blood and urine samples for laboratory assessments.
- Administer the [Quality of Life Questionnaire] and the [Patient Global Assessment] at the visits specified in the SoA.
- Record any changes in disease activity using the [Disease Activity Score] and [C-Reactive Protein] assessments.

**12.4 Follow-up Period (Week 52 to Week 56)**

The follow-up period begins after the last dose of investigational product. A follow-up visit will be conducted at Week 56, or at the time of early termination, during which the following procedures will be performed:

- Collect AE and SAE information.
- Review concomitant medications.
- Perform a physical examination and record vital signs.
- Collect blood and urine samples for laboratory assessments.
- Administer the [Quality of Life Questionnaire] and the [Patient Global Assessment].
- Record any changes in disease activity.
